sentences.text: Eisenbergiella tayi, the species for which the genus was proposed, is a catalase-positive, rod-shaped, non-proteolytic, non-motile, anaerobic bacterium of the family Lachnospiraceae.
Its type strain came from a blood culture of an 84-year-old male patient in Israel and produced butyrate, lactate, acetate and succinate as major metabolic end products.
Eight blood culture isolates and one appendix-derived isolate of Eisenbergiella tayi were recovered from seven patients in two Canadian provinces, and all had remarkably large genomes.
A further species, Eisenbergiella massiliensis, was isolated from a stool sample collected after bariatric surgery of an obese French woman.
